get.description: Returns every audit action string the server can emit, so the admin filter offers the full set instead of a hand-maintained subset.

post.description: Copies flows, settings and chat conversations from a legacy filesystem-backed server's data directory (PAD_DATA_DIR) into the database (admin only, deployments with a server store). Idempotent and non-blocking; the status result lists what is not migrated. Users are not migrated, so flows whose recorded owner is absent here are assigned to the admin who starts the run (reported as FlowsAdopted).

409.description: A migration is already running (on any replica)

503.description: Migration not configured, or its cross-replica lock is unavailable (try again)

get.description: Returns the status/result of the most recent data migration on any replica (admin only): the run and its result are recorded in the job state, so every replica answers alike.

post.description: Starts a governance sweep now (admin only): the scanner's periodic pass, run in the background; its alerts arrive as a scheduled sweep's do. 200 {started: true} once it has started. A sweep already running on this or another replica is a 409 with code SCAN_ALREADY_RUNNING (its results are the ones asked for). A server that is stopping answers 503 SERVER_RESTARTING with Retry-After; no server store to sweep, or the sweep's cross-replica lock unavailable, is a 503 SCAN_UNAVAILABLE (try again).

409.description: A sweep is already running (code SCAN_ALREADY_RUNNING)

503.description: The sweep could not start (code SCAN_UNAVAILABLE), or the server is stopping (code SERVER_RESTARTING)

get.description: The deployment-wide ai values: the daily budgets the budget gate enforces on every replica (0 = unlimited) and the embedding provider and model every knowledge base shares. Admin only.

put.description: Replaces the deployment-wide ai values with the body's and answers with what is now enforced. The body is the whole set of four fields: one it omits is written as zero (an unlimited budget, the server-default embedding provider or model), so send every field, changed or not. The rest of the deployment document is kept as stored, and a member's own settings write never reaches these fields. An embedding provider whose model ids are deployment aliases (Azure AI Foundry) is refused: it embeds only on the operator's PAD_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER pin. Admin only.

parameters.description: The values to enforce, all four
parameters.name: request

400.description: BAD_REQUEST: a negative budget, an embedding provider that cannot embed or needs the operator's pin, or an oversized model id

get.description: handleAdminSystemHealth returns a structured per-subsystem health breakdown. Admin-only (the public /readyz is the orchestrator-facing verdict). Reuses the same probes as readiness but reports each independently rather than collapsing to one pass/fail, and does NOT apply the consecutive-failure smoothing — an admin querying health wants the live picture, not a flap-dampened one. Also says which build (binaryVersion), schema migration (schemaVersion) and replica (instanceId) answered, which differ between replicas during a rolling deploy.

Returns one page of registered users, newest first, with the number of users matching the filters (total). hasMore reports users after the page, and nextCursor (absent on the last page) is the ?cursor= of the next one, with the same filters; a page with a cursor ignores offset. Only available to system admins.

post.description: Runs all enabled analysis rules on the current flow document.

handleAnalyzeRaw analyzes raw PAD flow text WITHOUT requiring a pre-stored flow, so CI pipelines and wrappers can POST flow text and get findings back in one call — no library upload, no Go CLI install. Works in both modes (auth via PAT in cloud; open in local). Body: {files, name, format?} where format is "json" (default: the analysis report), "sarif" (SARIF 2.1.0), "junit" (JUnit XML) or "csv"; those three are sent as an attachment named pad-analysis.<ext>. At most 50 files and 2048 KB in total. Nothing is persisted.

200.description: Analysis report (json), or the SARIF, JUnit or CSV document

400.description: Bad Request (no files, unknown format, parse failure)

413.description: Too many files or payload too large

The body is {rule, flowId} and nothing else; a rule the strict check refuses is a 400 with details.field ("rule.<field>") and details.reason. A built-in rule's id is not refused here (a legacy rule saved under one stays testable): it comes back in problems (reason RESERVED_ID, not a warning, since a save refuses it for a new rule), next to the strict check's warnings.

Each entry reports valid, its first error with field and reason, and every problem (problems; warning: true for one the rule runs with). A malformed document is a 400.

post.description: Changes the password for the currently authenticated user.

handleAuthForgotPassword issues a password-reset token and emails its link. It always responds 200 with the same body whether or not the email exists, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
Authenticates a user and returns access and refresh tokens.
Logs out the current user. In stateless JWT mode, this is primarily a client-side operation.

get.description: Returns information about the currently authenticated user: the claims' core, the stored profile (display name, avatar URL, account stamps) and, in cloud mode, the settings document's profile section (bio, job title, timezone). The web client reads that section from its settings store; it is here for other clients (the CLI, scripts) so they need no second call.

put.description: handleAuthUpdateProfile lets a user set their own display name and avatar URL. Both fields are optional and may be cleared by sending an empty string. The avatar URL is an http(s) URL, or the caller's own avatar route (/api/users/{id}/avatar) to keep an uploaded picture while changing the name; any other value, an empty one included, replaces the uploaded picture and deletes the stored image. The route without an upload behind it is a 400.

post.description: Re-encodes the uploaded PNG or JPEG (metadata stripped, a JPEG turned upright by its EXIF orientation, downscaled to at most 512 px, at most 512 KB stored), stores it as the caller's avatar and points the profile's avatar URL at the serving route. A multipart/form-data body with one "avatar" file part; the declared content type is never trusted — the bytes decide.

400.description: Not a PNG or JPEG image, or not a multipart form with an avatar part

post.description: Returns a new access token using a valid refresh token.
Creates a new user account with email and password.
Re-sends the verification link for a registered, still-unverified address. Always returns 200 so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which emails exist.
handleAuthResetPassword redeems a reset token and sets a new password, revoking all of the user's existing sessions.

get.summary: List active sessions for the current user

delete.description: handleAuthSessionRevoke revokes one of the caller's own sessions (refresh tokens) by ID, e.g. to sign out a lost device.

get.description: handleSSOCallback receives the IdP redirect, validates state, exchanges the code for a verified identity, finds or creates the local user, and bounces the browser back to the SPA with a short-lived single-use exchange ticket in the URL fragment (fragments are not sent to servers or logged).

post.description: handleSSOExchange swaps a single-use SSO ticket for a regular token pair — the SSO equivalent of handleAuthLogin's response.

get.description: handleSSOInfo tells the SPA whether to render the SSO login button.

get.summary: List the caller's linked SSO identities

delete.summary: Unlink an SSO identity from the current account

409.description: No password set — unlinking would lock the account

get.description: handleSSOStart begins the OIDC authorization-code flow: it stores the state/nonce/PKCE-verifier in an HttpOnly cookie and redirects the browser to the IdP.

get.summary: List API tokens for the current user

post.description: handleAuthVerifyEmail redeems an email-verification token and marks the user's email verified.
Signals the backend to start sending events for the specified stream ID.

Cancels an active streaming session. A stream that runs on another server of a multi-server deployment is stopped through that server; when it cannot be reached the answer is 503 with code REPLICA_UNREACHABLE (retry), never an ok that stopped nothing. A stream whose server has stopped running (it no longer renews its liveness record, about 15 seconds after it died) ended with it, and is answered like any ended stream (ok).

403.description: Not the stream's owner, or a stream mirrored by a server of the release before multi-server stop (code STREAM_NOT_FOUND; the client takes it as gone)

503.description: The stream runs on another server this one could not reach (code REPLICA_UNREACHABLE; Retry-After and details.retryAfterSeconds say when to retry; nothing is known to have been stopped)

post.description: Deletes the chat history for a specific flow and provider. With baseVersion the history is deleted only if the conversation still has that version, else 409 CONVERSATION_CONFLICT with details.version; without it the delete is unconditional, as before.

409.description: CONVERSATION_CONFLICT: the conversation is no longer at baseVersion (details.version is the current one)

post.description: Approval decision: delivers the user's approve/decline (with per-item opt-outs for a batch) for a tool request — a fix_proposal event — pending in one of the caller's chat streams. The stream must be the caller's, and a scoped API token must hold the scope the tool requires (write for the fix tools). First decision wins; unknown or already-decided proposals return 404, and so does a proposal whose server has stopped running (its stream ended with it).

403.description: Not the stream's owner (code STREAM_NOT_FOUND), or a token without the scope the tool requires

503.description: The stream runs on another server this one could not reach (code REPLICA_UNREACHABLE; Retry-After and details.retryAfterSeconds say when to retry; the decision may not have been delivered, so send it again)

post.description: Retrieves the chat history for a specific flow and conversation key (the wire field is historically named `provider`). The body is an object — {messages: [...]} (always an array), version (the conversation's version, 0 when none is stored yet; send it back as baseVersion on save and clear; absent where the store has no versions) plus activeStreamId when the caller has a stream on this conversation whose question is stored but whose answer is not yet (live, or finished and still being stored) — so a client that reloads mid-turn can re-attach via /api/chat/resume instead of losing the answer until another reload. The frontend still accepts the bare array older servers answered with.

Returns a preview of the context that will be sent to the AI provider: the system prompt, the context text, the user message, an estimate of their tokens and the model's context window. The model and the provider resolve as the turn's would: for provider azure-foundry a model registry id the caller cannot use is refused with 400 and code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE; a provider no spec describes with 400 PROVIDER_UNKNOWN; one the provider policy refuses (disabled in the deployment, or off the flow's organisation's allowed-provider list) with 400 PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED.

400.description: Bad Request: malformed body, code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE (the Azure AI Foundry model is not available to the caller), PROVIDER_UNKNOWN (no provider spec describes the id) or PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED (the provider policy refused it)

post.description: Reconnect to an in-flight AI stream and catch up on missed chunks. A stream the server does not know — it restarted without the resume backplane, the stream finished more than two minutes ago, or it is another user's — answers code STREAM_NOT_FOUND: 403 with accounts (an unknown stream and another user's are not told apart), 404 without. The client reports such a stream as interrupted.

403.description: Unknown stream, or another user's (code STREAM_NOT_FOUND; with accounts)

post.description: Saves the chat history for a specific flow and provider. A message's modelLabel (the model's display name when it was sent) is stored clamped: NFC-normalised, control, bidi and zero-width characters dropped, whitespace collapsed, at most 64 characters. With baseVersion (the version GET returned, or a previous save answered) the list replaces the stored one only if the conversation still has that version, and the response carries the new version; a conversation that changed since answers 409 CONVERSATION_CONFLICT with details.version (the current version): reload, merge by message id and save again. Without baseVersion (a client from before versions) the save replaces the stored list whatever it holds, which can erase a turn another tab or the server stored; it is counted in pad_chat_blind_saves_total.

409.description: CONVERSATION_CONFLICT: the conversation is no longer at baseVersion (details.version is the current one)

post.description: Initiates a streaming chat session with an AI provider. The answer arrives on the event stream as chunk, tool, tool_result, done and error events. The done payload carries tokensIn, tokensOut and chunks, plus — when known — servedModel (the model that answered an alias such as an Azure AI Foundry deployment, router or agent) and inputCostPerM / outputCostPerM (the per-million-token rates the turn was billed at). When the server stored the turn itself (cloud mode, the request carried no history) the answer is in the store before done is sent, and done and error also carry conversationVersion (the stored conversation's version after the server's own writes) and conversationBase (the version the turn began from), only while no other writer changed the thread in between; a client still at conversationBase can adopt conversationVersion without saving or reloading. An error payload carries message and, when classified, code (AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, AI_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE, PROVIDER_AUTH, PROVIDER_PERMISSION, PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED, PROVIDER_UNKNOWN when the turn names a provider no spec describes, PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED when the provider policy refused it — disabled in the deployment or off the organisation's allowed-provider list (ADR 0028), MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, SERVER_RESTARTING when the server's stop ended the stream, …). A provider id the registry does not know is refused before any stream starts with 400 and code PROVIDER_UNKNOWN. For provider azure-foundry the model is a model registry id ("m/<entryId>"; "" for the server default; a pre-registry deployment, "claude:" or "agent:" id still resolves for one release): one the caller cannot use — removed, another owner's, no longer shared with them — is refused before any stream starts with 400 and code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE. While the server is stopping no stream starts: 503 with code SERVER_RESTARTING, a Retry-After header and details.retryAfterSeconds; the request may be sent again once after that wait. A clientStreamId that already names a stream (running, or finished within the resume window, on any replica) is refused with 409 and code STREAM_ID_IN_USE: a resent start whose first send went through gets it, and resumes that stream (POST /api/chat/resume) instead of starting another.

400.description: Bad Request: malformed body, code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE (the Azure AI Foundry model is not available to the caller) or PROVIDER_UNKNOWN (no provider spec describes the id)

409.description: The clientStreamId already names a stream (code STREAM_ID_IN_USE): resume it

429.description: Too many concurrent chat streams (code CHAT_CAPACITY_REACHED)

503.description: The server is restarting (code SERVER_RESTARTING; Retry-After and details.retryAfterSeconds say when to send it again)

post.description: Returns suggested prompts based on the current flow state.

get.description: Every section is computed for the same scope and window. Findings filters (severity, category, rule) map each flow's per-rule counts through the current rule catalog.
get.summary: Filterable analytics for the Analytics page

parameters.description: IANA time zone for day bucketing (default UTC)
parameters.name: tz

get.summary: Aggregated dashboard data for the home view

get.description: Long-lived SSE channel for analysis, chat, and collaboration events. Chunks stream incrementally. On a deployment with a shared Redis (several replicas) every event except chat chunks, heartbeats and progress ticks carries an `id:` line, and a client that reconnects with Last-Event-ID is replayed the frames it missed (at most 200, from the last 5 minutes) before the live stream continues. A reconnect the log cannot replay whole (more frames missed, a cursor older than the log, or the log unreadable) gets one `replay:gap` event instead of a partial replay, which tells the client to refetch what it shows; without Redis the frames carry no id and the header is ignored, so a client refetches what it needs after a reconnect. While the server is stopping a new stream is refused with 503 and code SERVER_RESTARTING (Retry-After); one already open stays open until the server has delivered the chat streams' terminal events.

parameters.description: The id of the last frame the client received; replays what followed it (needs the shared Redis, else ignored)
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

503.description: The server is restarting (code SERVER_RESTARTING; reconnect after Retry-After), or too many connections

Renders the flow's current analysis report as a self-contained HTML page and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.

Renders the flow's current analysis report as Markdown and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.

Renders the flow's current analysis report as a PDF and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.
Desktop only. Writes the findings panel's CSV, or the SARIF / JUnit text it fetched, to the absolute path chosen in the native save dialog (.csv, .sarif or .xml only). 403 in cloud mode.

handleApplyFix applies a deterministic auto-fix (e.g. wrap-in-error-handler) to a block in the flow's source file, re-parses, and returns the updated document. Desktop/local only. The finding carries the available fixType in its AutoFix field; the frontend shows "Apply fix" only when that is set.

handleApplyFixBatch applies multiple auto-fixes in one pass (iterative loop, persisted once). The frontend's bulk-action bar derives the rule set from the selected findings; the server fixes every auto-fixable finding whose rule is in that set (re-parsing between fixes so line shifts don't corrupt targets).

get.description: Returns a list of recently opened flow documents.

Performs a search for text or patterns within a specific flow document.

handleSearchLibrary runs a query across every flow the caller can access (cross-flow / org-wide search), merging per-flow hits into one result set. Each hit is stamped with its source flowId/flowName so the UI can group them. The text needs a run of at least 3 letters or digits; an empty text answers no results.

400.description: BAD_REQUEST, or QUERY_TOO_SHORT (no run of 3 letters or digits; details.minLength)

delete.description: handleClearGovernanceAlerts — DELETE /api/governance/alerts Permanently removes the caller's visible dismissed alerts.

get.description: handleUnreadGovernanceAlertCount — GET /api/governance/alerts/unread-count Returns {"count": N} for the bell badge (lighter than listing).

Returns 200 when downstream dependencies (DB) are reachable, 503 otherwise. While the server is stopping it answers 503 {"status":"draining"} from the first probe on, whatever its dependencies say. A dependency that is down but not needed to serve (the Redis backplane) does not fail the probe: the 200 body then lists it as {"status":"ok","degraded":["redis"]}.

200.description: OK; degraded lists the optional dependencies that are down

503.description: Service Unavailable (status draining while the server stops)

post.description: Analyzes a stored flow for a CI runner. Authenticated by an HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-Baki-Timestamp>." + body, sent as X-Baki-Signature: sha256=<hex>; the timestamp must be within 5 minutes. The key is an organisation CI credential (baki_ci_<keyId>_<secret>, minted under /api/orgs/{id}/ci-credentials; send X-Baki-Key-Id: <keyId>), which reaches that organisation's flows only, or the deprecated deployment-wide PAD_CI_WEBHOOK_SECRET (answered with Deprecation and Link headers where organisations exist). Instead of a signature, Authorization: Bearer <API token> with the ci scope reaches the flows the token's user can read, an organisation's flow only when the user is a member of it; an unscoped token or one without ci is a 401, and another user's flow is a 404 like an unknown one. Body: {flowId, failOn, format, deliveryId}. failOn is error (default), warning, info or none; findings of preview rules never fail the gate and are counted in `preview`. format "summary" (default) returns {flowId, flowName, passed, gate, errors, warnings, info, preview}, "report" adds the findings, "sarif" returns the SARIF 2.1.0 document instead (application/sarif+json); a missing or empty format is "summary", any other is a 400 with code UNKNOWN_FORMAT and details.formats listing the three. deliveryId (16 to 128 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _; bakicli sends 128 random bits) makes the call run once per key: a call whose key sent the same deliveryId before is a 409 CI_REPLAYED and runs nothing. It is optional for now.

parameters.description: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp.body>; required without Authorization
parameters.name: X-Baki-Signature

parameters.description: Key id of the organisation CI credential
parameters.name: X-Baki-Key-Id

parameters.description: Bearer <API token with the ci scope>, instead of a signature
parameters.name: Authorization

200.description: Gate verdict, or the SARIF document

400.description: Bad Request (no flowId, malformed deliveryId; code UNKNOWN_FORMAT with details.formats for an unknown format)

401.description: Missing or invalid signature, key, timestamp or API token

404.description: Flow not found (or outside what the credential or token reaches)

409.description: CI_REPLAYED: this key already sent the deliveryId

503.description: Not configured (no accounts and no PAD_CI_WEBHOOK_SECRET), or no server store

post.description: handleInviteAccept redeems an invite token, adding the calling user to the invite's organisation with the role specified in the invite.

Deletes an API key for a given provider. For azure-foundry (deprecated form, one release): removes the caller's resource "default" — the migrated single-document configuration — with its models and its stored credential; the other resources stay (DELETE /api/providers/azure-foundry/connections/{connectionId} removes one).

400.description: Malformed body, or a provider id no spec describes (PROVIDER_UNKNOWN)

post.description: Checks if an API key for a given provider is saved. For azure-foundry (deprecated form, one release): whether the caller has at least one Azure AI Foundry resource of their own — GET /api/providers/azure-foundry/connections lists them.

400.description: Malformed body, or a provider id no spec describes (PROVIDER_UNKNOWN)

post.description: Saves an API key for a given provider.

400.description: Malformed body, a provider id no spec describes (PROVIDER_UNKNOWN), or a provider configured through its own routes rather than a bare key (USE_PROVIDER_CONFIG: azure-foundry, local)

get.description: Returns one page of the flows visible to the caller, with optional filtering by organization, scope, name and tags. total counts the matching flows up to 10 000; totalCapped is true when more match. A page reached by cursor reports the total the first page counted (its cursor carries it). hasMore reports flows after the page that the client can reach. With the updated-at sorts the page carries nextCursor (absent on the last page, and on a page reached by offset whose flows' ids are all too long for a cursor: then page on by offset): pass it as ?cursor= with the same filters and sort for the next page, which then ignores offset; cursors reach every flow. Without a cursor the page starts at offset, at most 10 000 (hasMore is false where the next offset would pass it), so the name and block sorts reach offsets up to and including 10 000 (so 10 000 + one page by offset).

post.description: One route for a saved or draft resource and a saved or draft model: {connectionId} tests a saved resource, {config} a draft one — with connectionId too, the stored secret carries over by the same host rules as a save — and model ({id} of a saved model, or a draft {kind, deployment}) tests a model on that resource. A resource test signs in and probes the endpoint (and the project) with no model call, at no cost; a chat, Claude or embedding model test sends one tiny request Azure bills; an agent test only looks the agent up — it is never run. Drafts write nothing; a saved target records its last test. Every test outcome is a 200 {ok, latencyMs, error?, code?}; a 4xx only means an invalid request. Strict body, at most 64 KiB. Rides the chat rate-limit bucket.

post.description: Validates and stores the base URL of a locally hosted OpenAI-compatible server and, optionally, the context window history is trimmed to (omitted or 0 = 8192 tokens; else 1024..2000000). post.description: Tests the connection to a specific AI provider with one tiny billed chat call per candidate model. Every outcome is a 200 {ok, latencyMs, error?, code?}; code names a refusal the client branches on: PROVIDER_UNKNOWN (no such provider), PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED (the provider policy refused it: disabled in this deployment — this route tests the caller's own credential, so the organisation's allowed-provider list applies to the org test route, POST /api/orgs/{id}/providers/azure-foundry/test, instead), AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED / AI_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE (the daily AI budget gates the test like any other call — nothing was sent). For azure-foundry this form is deprecated (one release): it tests the caller's resource "default" (else their first resource) as a resource — an authenticated probe, no model call; use POST /api/providers/azure-foundry/test to test one resource or model.

Returns 200 when downstream dependencies (DB) are reachable, 503 otherwise. While the server is stopping it answers 503 {"status":"draining"} from the first probe on, whatever its dependencies say. A dependency that is down but not needed to serve (the Redis backplane) does not fail the probe: the 200 body then lists it as {"status":"ok","degraded":["redis"]}.

200.description: OK; degraded lists the optional dependencies that are down

503.description: Service Unavailable (status draining while the server stops)

id or by anchor), "missing" (no longer in the flow; the context says so) or "" (none asked for).

SupportsTools reports whether the provider family behind this model
supports the agentic tool loop. Provider-level granularity: mixed
